name: python-keyset-pagination
title: Python keyset pagination
blurb: Pagination where a row can be neither skipped nor repeated: the cursor names a position (`(sort_key, id) > (?, ?)`) instead of counting rows, so a deleted row behind the cursor cannot shift the next page, an insert cannot make it repeat one, and a cursor carries the fingerprint of the query it was made for — a `demo` walks both mutations and exits 1 while LIMIT/OFFSET still loses a row
default_description: Cursor pagination over SQLite with composite keys, opaque query-bound cursors, and a demo that shows what OFFSET costs.
